must_remember: A wavefront is the locus of all adjacent points in a medium vibrating in the same phase.
The direction of propagation of light (ray) is always perpendicular to the wavefront at any point.
Every point on a given wavefront acts as a secondary source of light, emitting secondary wavelets in all directions.
The frequency of light remains completely invariant when it crosses an optical boundary between two different media.
The back-propagation of secondary wavelets is non-existent or has zero amplitude due to the obliquity factor.

glossary.meaning: The locus of all adjacent points in a medium vibrating in the same phase.
Spherical wavelets emitted by every point on a primary wavefront according to Huygens' principle.
A directional factor $1 + \cos(\theta)$ that accounts for the absence of back-propagation in Huygens' construction.
The ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in a given medium ($n = c/v$).
